div.note: MS G (Cotton Nero A I, f. 92v, after V Atr., in the same hand c. 1070); the heading is decorated in red. Liebermann dates Grið 1028–1070 and thinks the author was perhaps a Kentishman. K is the same manuscript as the modern edition.; T: corrected against Rabin p. 22, October 2026 (was “7; munde.”, now “and; munde”); U: corrected against Rabin p. 23, October 2026 (was “Concerning Sanctuary and Protection”, now “Concerning Sanctuary and Protection (expanded letters in italics: Concerning Sanctuary and Protection)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “1028–1070; before 1014 (Wormald); 1006–8 (Rabin)”, now “1028–1070 (Liebermann); before 1014 (Wormald); 1006–8 (Rabin)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “1028–1070 (Liebermann); before 1014 (Wormald); 1006–8 (Rabin)”, now “1028–1070 (Liebermann, I p. 470); before 1014 (Wormald, MEL pp. 394–5); 1006–8 (Rabin)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “G 470; German 470”; 39 rows of Grið)

Thompson Hydrosulphur freundlich anwendete, mehr als 1901; was mir April 1902 G. F. Warner gütig mittheilte, notire ich dankend.

MS Nero A I f. 96v., after VIII Atr. 5, 2, above p. 264⁵, hand of c. 1070. Erasures, wear and chemicals make the text partly illegible. I once saw more, when E. M. Thompson kindly applied hydrosulphur, than in 1901; what G. F. Warner kindly communicated to me in April 1902 I record with thanks.
